Summary: Reports the EntraOps findings on privileged access in Maester: Enterprise Access Model tier breaches, standing access, account protection, workload identities, PIM activation and approval, access packages, access drift from access packages (Access Guardian) and changes between snapshots. EntraOps evaluates the checks; the pack reads its results (findings.json) and needs no connection, no permission and no module.

Prerequisites.Text: PowerShell 7.4 or later and Maester 3.0 or later.

EntraOps 1.2.0 or later, which evaluates the checks and saves the results to findings.json: Invoke-EntraOpsAssessment (without EntraOps in place) or New-EntraOpsReportingData (in an EntraOps repository). The EntraOps reporting pipelines (GitHub Actions and Azure DevOps) publish it in the EntraOps-Reporting artifact (Findings/data/findings.json). Until EntraOps 1.2.0 is on the PowerShell Gallery, import the module from a clone of the EntraOps Insiders repository (Import-Module ./EntraOps/EntraOps.psd1).

The results in Reports/Findings/data of the EntraOps working folder (ENTRAOPS_ROOT, <home>/EntraOps or the current folder), or the EntraOps.FindingsPath setting in maester-config.json for another location.

Steps.Text: Without EntraOps in place: run a complete EntraOps assessment, which saves the results to Reports/Findings/data/findings.json of the EntraOps working folder.
With an EntraOps repository: generate the reports and the results in your clone, or download the newest EntraOps-Reporting artifact and set EntraOps.FindingsPath to its Findings/data folder.

Notes: The pack only reads findings.json; it does not call Microsoft Graph or any other service.

When Microsoft Graph is connected (by Maester or earlier in the session), results of another tenant are skipped; with -SkipGraphConnect the tenant cannot be compared, so each result names the tenant and the date of the EntraOps results. Results older than EntraOps.MaxFindingsAgeDays (default 7) are skipped too.

Commands.Text: Only this pack, without connecting to Microsoft Graph

Only this pack, with the affected objects (users, groups, service principals, Conditional Access policies, access packages) and their EntraOps tier on Maester's Affected objects page: collected by default since Maester 3.0.0-rc73, with -IncludeAffectedObjects in earlier previews

Options.Name: EntraOps.FindingsPath
Options.Text: The findings.json of EntraOps, or the folder that holds it (for example ./EntraOps-Reporting/Findings/data). Without it, the pack reads Reports/Findings/data of ENTRAOPS_ROOT, <home>/EntraOps or the current folder.
Options.Default: Reports/Findings/data of the EntraOps working folder

Options.Name: EntraOps.MaxFindingsAgeDays
Options.Text: Results older than this are skipped. 0 turns the check off.

Options.Name: EntraOps.ReportsPath
Options.Default: The reports two folders above findings.json, when they are there
Options.Text: Where the results link to the EntraOps reports (Findings view, Tier Breach Analyzer, EAM Dashboard, Access Path Map, PIM Request Flow, Access Package Flow, Conditional Access Analysis, Configuration Analyzer): the URL where they are published (https://...) or their folder. A folder becomes a link that opens from a Maester report opened from disk. None turns the links off. The objects are linked to the Microsoft Entra admin center either way.

Options.Name: EntraOpsConfig.json: Findings
Options.Text: Excluded rules and the thresholds of the checks are set in EntraOps, which evaluates the checks (Findings section of EntraOpsConfig.json, see https://www.entraops.com/docs/reportings/index.html#findings). Excluded rules are skipped here.

Options.Name: EntraOpsConfig.json: Findings.EmergencyAccessAccounts
Options.Text: Set this first, with the object IDs or user principal names of your emergency access accounts and their group: their permanent Control Plane role assignments are then not reported by MP.EOPS.3001, and Conditional Access policies that exclude them don't fail MP.EOPS.4003. Without it, MP.EOPS.4003 reports every excluded Control Plane user, and its reason names the users excluded from every enabled policy as candidates for the setting.

Options.Name: EntraOps Finding Exceptions File
Options.Text: Dismissed and risk-accepted findings are exceptions in EntraOps (Findings.ExceptionsFilePath, maintained in the Findings view of the Privileged Assets report). Dismissed findings (false positives) pass a test; a test with risk-accepted findings and no open one is skipped with the accepted risks as the reason. Expired exceptions report their findings again. See https://www.entraops.com/docs/reportings/index.html#finding-exceptions.

AppOnly.Text: The pack needs no permission and no connection. In a pipeline, download the EntraOps-Reporting artifact and run Invoke-Maester -Pack EOPS -SkipBuiltIn -SkipGraphConnect -NonInteractive, or connect Maester as usual to run it with Maester's own tests.
